'''Philip George Burke FRS'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Hibbert|first=Alan|date=2021|title=Philip George Burke. 18 October 1932—4 June 2019|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=70|pages=57–77 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0043 |s2cid=232326782 |doi-access=free}}</ref> (18 October 1932—4 June 2019) was a British theoretical and [[Computational physics|computational physicist]] who developed the R-matrix method for studying electron collisions with atoms and molecules.

== Life ==
He was born in London. He graduated from  University College of the South West, and University College London. He worked at the National Physical Laboratory, Teddington. From 1959 to 1960, he worked at the Lawrence Berkeley Radiation Laboratory.<ref name=":0" />

The majority of Burke's research career was based at [[Queen's University Belfast]], where he was a member of the Centre for Theoretical Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics.

He was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1978 and was awarded a [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in 1993.
